notes: Golden and bad samples for every text check in this suite. validate.py asserts each golden satisfies every check in its block and each bad sample trips at least one. write_content probes are the content ARGUMENT of write_memory: for append-rule-not-rewrite that is the delta only, which is why its golden is one numbered item and its bad sample is the whole retyped checklist. Several of these were written before the checks and changed them. The stale threshold is graded by REGEX, not substring — '30 days' as a literal missed the hyphenated '30-day' that a correct-sounding rewrite reaches for, so update-skill-in-place and write-skill-not-topic both use \b30[\s-]*days?\b (forbidden) and \b90[\s-]*days?\b (required); the update bad sample is deliberately a near-golden that differs from the golden ONLY by the '(previously 30 days)' parenthetical plus the truncation, so the regex has to be what separates them. Every must_not_match naming a report shape is tempered with negative lookbehinds for 'not ' / "n't " / 'never ' — 'I have not created a new skill' is the CORRECT answer to two of these tasks and an untempered pattern fails it, which is the exact bug that was already caught once here on the loose 'a new skill' form.

write_content.golden:
# Refreshing a Stale Topic

## 1. Decide it is actually stale
A topic is stale when its frontmatter timestamp is more than 90 days old.
"Feels old" is not a threshold. Inside 90 days, leave the note alone and say
why you left it.

## 2. Refresh in place, never alongside
Call write_memory with item_id set to the existing topics/....md id. A write
with no item_id creates a SECOND topic — the failure this skill exists for.
It happened to the kimi-k3 note twice, and both times the agent reported that
it had updated the topic.

## 3. Carry forward what the new source does not contradict
The new page restates some facts, changes some, and quietly drops others.
Anything the old note carried that the new source does not contradict has to
survive the refresh. Pasting the new page over the old body deletes the facts
the new source simply did not mention.

## 4. Report the diff, not the act
"Updated the topic" is not a report. Name what changed — old value, new value
— and name what stayed the same.

## 5. Refuse when the source no longer matches
If the source_url 404s, redirects to a parked domain, or now covers a
different subject, do NOT refresh. Leave the note untouched and tell the
operator what that URL serves today.

# Tool Result Verification Checklist

1. **Read the status field.** `already_ingested`, `exists`, `queued` and
   `following` are not `written`.
2. **Quote the id back.** When a result carries an `id`, put that id in your
   answer.
3. **Treat `Error:` as a stop, not a hint.** A result beginning `Error:` or
   `Blocked by rule` means nothing happened.
4. **Count what the tool counted.** If the result says `queued: 10`, say
   queued.
5. **Never narrate a call you did not make.**
6. **Repeat the warning.** A `warning` alongside a successful status names
   the item_id; repeat it and fix the item in the same turn.

write_content.golden:
## Name the failure modes
Say what a failure looks like from the caller's side. Every builtin returns a
string, so a failure arrives as text beginning `Error:` — not an exception,
not an empty result. Say what that error means for the next step: retry with
different arguments, ask the operator, or stop. And say what the tool does
not do even when it succeeds — follow_source queues a backfill, it does not
ingest one.

## Say when NOT to reach for it
Name the adjacent tool and the line between them: "use this for a channel or
playlist page; for a single video use ingest_media instead." A description
that only says what a tool is for leaves the model guessing at the boundary,
and the guess costs a wasted round.

write_content.golden:
# Writing a Description That Earns Its Line

## The rule
A skill's description says what the skill is FOR. If every word in it already
appears in the title, the catalogue treats it as no description at all and
drops it from the listing — so a description that restates the title costs a
line and teaches nothing.

## How to tell
Strike out every word the title already contains, plus stopwords. Three or
fewer words left and you wrote an echo. "Guidance skill: guidance for skills"
is an echo. "Five checks to run on a tool result before writing a sentence
that depends on it" is not.

## Why it matters
The catalogue is how an agent finds a skill it did not know to search for. A
row that reads as its own title gives it nothing to choose on.
